sections.heading: MALFEASANCE IN PUBLIC OFFICE
sections.chapter_heading: CRIMES OF GROSS ABUSES OF POWER AND AUTHORITY.
sections.text: (1)Any government officer who intentionally incorrectly or unlawfully abuses their office in a manner that endangers the life or freedom, as guaranteed by statute or the Constitution of the United States, of another, shall be guilty of malfeasance in public office. (2)This shall be a Class B Offense. (3)For the purposes of this offense, a “government officer” shall be any individual who is elected, appointed, or otherwise employed by the government at any level.

sections.heading: ABUSE OF OFFICIAL CAPACITY
sections.chapter_heading: CRIMES OF GROSS ABUSES OF POWER AND AUTHORITY.
sections.text:
(1) Any public servant with the intent to benefit, defraud, or harm another: (a) Violates a law related to the public servant’s employment; (b)Misuses government or city property, services, personnel, or anything of value that has come to the public servant’s possession through their employment. (c) Uses emergency signals such as lights for personal benefit such as speeding, parking, or crossing over land without an immediate emergency to respond to; (d)Uses the tazer on another player whether it be a playful or other way without the requirement of such force; (e) Uses a vehicle to purposely block off an area without the appropriate authority or reasoning to do such; or (f) Detains someone without lawful reason and instead for a trivial reason, Shall be guilty of Abuse of official capacity.
(2)This shall be a class B offense.

sections.heading: FALSE IMPRISONMENT
sections.chapter_heading: CRIMES OF GROSS ABUSES OF POWER AND AUTHORITY.
sections.text: (1)Any law enforcement officer, or other person holding the ability to make arrests without warrant, and deliberately—. (a) Imprisons another person without legal basis; (b)Executes an arrest warrant more than the permitted times; or (c) Imprisons someone with reason but under the incorrect arrest type or code, Shall be guilty of False imprisonment. (2)This shall be a Class B offense.

sections.heading: PUBLIC CORRUPTION
sections.chapter_heading: CRIMES OF GROSS ABUSES OF POWER AND AUTHORITY.
sections.text: (1)Any person who immorally misuses or abuses a government office, as prescribed by law, for personal gain and benefit in a malicious manner, shall be guilty of Public corruption. (2)Any person who immorally misuses or abuses a government office, as prescribed by law, for personal gain in a malicious manner, and endangers the life of another whilst doing so, shall be guilty of Public corruption. (3)This shall be a Class C offense.

sections.heading: MALICIOUS PROSECUTION
sections.chapter_heading: CRIMES OF GROSS ABUSES OF POWER AND AUTHORITY.
sections.text: (1)Any person who proceeds with the wrongful institution of criminal proceedings against another person without reasonable grounds and/or uses their prosecutorial office for their own personal or pecuniary gain, or the personal and pecuniary gain of another, shall be guilty of Malicious prosecution. (2)This shall be a Class A offense.

sections.heading: ILLEGAL DISCHARGE OF NON-LETHAL WEAPON
sections.chapter_heading: CRIMES OF GROSS ABUSES OF POWER AND AUTHORITY.
sections.text:
(1)Any person possessing a non-lethal weapon, whether it be automatic or manual, illegal or legal and discharging it without being attacked by another player, provocation or being in imminent danger; for purposes of pleasure or self-gain or other perverted desire, shall be guilty of illegal discharge of a non-lethal weapon. (2)This shall be a Class D offense. (3)For the purposes of this offense, a “Non-lethal weapon” means a taser, pepper spray, tear gas, flash bangs, police baton, or other
weaponry which is not intended to cause great bodily harm when used appropriately.
